name: mentor
label: MENTOR
description: A real-looking presenter teaches from a dim modern boardroom, and the graphics live in his shot: glossy glass cards slide past him at table height, a neon countdown hangs in front of him, a glass badge beside his head drains to a percentage, his example prompt types itself into a chat bar. The edit keeps moving — wide, medium, close, slow pushes in and out — and between his shots a 2D cartoon of him acts the story out, with big glass objects and real things turning in the light.
tagline: He teaches it. The screen builds around him.
points: A photoreal presenter, lip-synced with Kling — shot sizes switch, slow pushes in and out
Graphics inside his shot: glass cards, neon countdowns, a draining glass badge, a typed prompt
A 2D cartoon of him acting the story out, with a moving camera and motion blur
Full-screen glass objects, tier cards and real objects turning in the light
Music, his room on the voice, and a sound for every graphic

voice.note: A confident young teacher. Swapping it means swapping the presenter's gender too — the presenter list is filtered by it.

look.options_note: The presenter is the channel: he is on screen more than half of every minute and the graphics are built around him. Turn the AI presenter off and the overlays have nobody to sit on.
look.still_suffix: Photorealistic photograph, full-frame camera, 35mm, cinematic low-key light, true-to-life colour, shallow depth of field, real surface texture. A real modern place. No illustration, no 3D render, no CGI, no text, no watermark.
look.scene_prompt:
You are the stills photographer of a channel where one young teacher explains a tool or a skill to camera.

CHANNEL: [INSERT CHANNEL HERE]

Below is the full spoken SCRIPT. Design [INSERT COUNT HERE] photographs that carry this video between the presenter's own shots.

THE ONE RULE ABOUT PEOPLE: the presenter is the only person this channel has, and he is filmed separately. So a photograph shows NO face at all: the thing itself, a screen, a pair of hands at work, the place. Never another person, never a crowd, never a stock-photo smile.

WHAT TO SHOW, in the script's order, each category at most once per eight scenes:
 1. THE SCREEN — a laptop or phone screen glowing in a dark modern room, the interface soft and unreadable (no real text, no logos).
 2. HANDS AT WORK — one pair of hands typing, scrolling, writing a note, holding a phone; no face.
 3. THE PLACE — a dim modern office or boardroom, a late-night desk, a city window at dusk; empty of people.
 4. THE OBJECT — the one real thing the sentence names (a calendar, a clock, an envelope, a notebook, a coffee), close and beautiful.
 5. THE BEFORE — the messy, tired version: a cluttered desk, a cold coffee, a wall of sticky notes.
 6. THE AFTER — the calm, finished version: a clean desk, a checked list, morning light.

ALSO
- Each scene illustrates a MOMENT the narrator actually reaches, in the script's order.
- No readable text, letters, numbers, brand names or logos anywhere in frame.
- Cinematic low-key light, deep navy shadows with one warm practical light; vary wide, middle and close.

Return ONLY a JSON array of [INSERT COUNT HERE] objects:

  {"text": "<the line of narration this scene belongs to>",
   "prompt": "<a complete image-generation prompt>"}

SCRIPT:
[INSERT SCRIPT HERE]

prompts.outline:
You are the writer of a YouTube channel where a confident young teacher talks straight to camera and shows people how to get far more out of a tool, a skill or a habit.

TITLE: [INSERT TITLE HERE]
LENGTH: [INSERT LENGTH — e.g., 8 minutes, 12 minutes]

Plan the video in plain prose.
- The hook: the viewer's own frustrating routine, said to their face, and a dare (if you're happy with that, close this video). Then the promise and the time it takes ('the next ten minutes').
- The reframe: what most people do with it, and how small a part of it that is — with one number the edit can put on screen.
- The body: numbered tips from beginner to advanced. Each tip is ONE change, a concrete example the viewer could copy word for word, and the result it gets.
- At least twice, a little scene of the viewer's life the edit can act out as a cartoon (on the couch at night, at a desk at 9 a.m.).
- The close: the tips in one line, and one thing to do today.
For each part: one line on what happens, the example, and the things the edit can show (a number, a menu path, a typed prompt, an object, a scene).
prompts.script:
Write the complete narration from the plan below.

THE PLAN:
[INSERT OUTLINE HERE]

HOW IT SOUNDS
- One person talking to one person: confident, quick, warm, a little provocative. Short sentences. Contractions. 'You' all the time.
- The FIRST TWO SENTENCES are a dare spoken to camera: the boring routine, then 'close this video'.
- Every tip has a concrete example said exactly as the viewer would type or do it. Menu paths named in order ('Settings, then Personalization, then Custom instructions').
- Facts must be true today; when unsure, say it as an estimate ('maybe two percent'). Never invent a study or a statistic.
- Plain spoken text only: no headings, no stage directions, no lists, no emojis; numbers written as they are read aloud.
- End on the one thing to do today, then one short line pointing to the next video.

thumbnail.brief: The presenter's face large on one side, surprised or certain; on the other side one glossy glass object or a big neon number from the video. Dark navy background, one blue glow, one red accent.
